newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia floods prompt state of emergency.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia floods prompt state of emergency.

text.p: Cambodia has declared a state of emergency in three eastern provinces after severe flooding, government officials said on Tuesday.
The affected provinces are Stung Treng, Kratie and Kompong Cham, the officials said. The Mekong River passes through all three.
"This year is very strange, the water is rising a month earlier than it usually does," Lim Keanhor, director of the agriculture ministry's irrigation department, told Reuters.
There were no reports of casualties and the officials said it was too early to assess damage to crops.
Typhoon Victor, which hit southern China on the weekend, also dumped significant amounts of rain over Cambodia.
